name: Deploy a real-time endpoint (SageMaker)
desc: Stand up a serverless endpoint, invoke it live, then clean up — with the instance + stop/start variant

cells.code:
## ☁️ Deploy a real-time endpoint

Everything else in the ML recipes is **batch**: train a model, score a table. Some consumers instead need **real-time** inference — a standing HTTPS model they can call one row at a time, from anywhere, by name, without loading scikit-learn or the model file themselves. That's a SageMaker **endpoint**.

Deploy **serverless by default**: it **scales to zero, costs $0 while idle**, and you pay only per request — no instance to babysit. The same custom serving container handles a `train_model` Pipeline, an ONNX export, or a SageMaker-trained model, all taking RAW rows.

```mermaid
graph LR
  M["trained model"] --> D["sm_deploy_serverless (wait=False)"]
  D --> PK["model.tar.gz → S3"]
  D --> EP["endpoint: Creating…"]
  EP -->|sm_endpoint_status| IS{"InService?"}
  IS -->|no · wait ~30s · re-run| IS
  IS -->|yes| INV["sm_predict / predict(ep, rows)"]
  INV --> R["live predictions"]
  EP -. $0 idle, pay per request .-> COST["serverless"]
  IS ==>|when done| DEL["sm_delete_endpoint"]
```

**⚠️ An endpoint is a STANDING resource** — unlike the rest of the recipes, it persists until you delete it. `sm_deploy_serverless(wait=False)` returns a handle immediately (like `sm_train`); you then **poll `sm_endpoint_status` until InService** (a serverless cold start is a few minutes). The last cell deletes it — that step is **not optional**.

### Serverless vs instance

| | `sm_deploy_serverless` (default) | `sm_deploy_instance` |
|---|---|---|
| Compute | scales to zero | dedicated, always-warm (incl. GPU types) |
| Cost | **$0 idle**, pay per request | **bills continuously** while running |
| Bring-up (deploy → InService) | a few min, **variable** (managed-pool cold pull) | a few min, **predictable** — often **faster** |
| First-invoke cold start | yes, after idle (auto-retried) | none once InService |
| Pause | n/a (already $0 idle) | `sm_stop_endpoint` → `sm_start_endpoint` |

**Don't be surprised if the instance endpoint reaches `InService` faster.** It's counterintuitive, but the slow part of either deploy is pulling our serving container image; serverless does that against a managed pool whose first-activation is slower and more variable, while an instance does a direct pull onto dedicated hardware. Serverless then *also* cold-starts on the first invoke after idling (why `sm_predict` auto-retries that), whereas an instance has no per-invoke cold start once warm. The payoff for serverless is **$0 idle**, not fast bring-up.

Reach for `sm_deploy_instance` when you truly need always-warm/GPU latency or fast, repeatable bring-up (e.g. a tight test loop) — and remember to **stop it** when idle.

# 1) Start from a trained model. Any of these work — the serving container dispatches
#    on the artifact:
#      • a train_model Pipeline (shown here)
#      • an ONNX export:            ep = sm_deploy_serverless(to_onnx(model, df.head(1)))
#      • a SageMaker-trained model: ep = sm_deploy_serverless(sm_load_model(job))
#    Reach for an endpoint only when a STANDING, callable-from-anywhere model is
#    actually needed (otherwise predict_batch in the VM is simpler and free).
model = train_model(
    read_athena("SELECT * FROM <your_table> LIMIT 5000"),
    target="<target_column>",
)

# 2) Deploy SERVERLESS (the default). wait=False returns a handle immediately so the
#    cell doesn't block on the few-minute cold start — poll it in the next cell.
ep = sm_deploy_serverless(model, name="<endpoint-name>", wait=False)
print("deploying:", ep.name, "·", ep.status())

# 3) POLL until InService — RE-RUN this cell every ~30s ('Creating' → 'InService',
#    or 'Failed: <reason>'). Only invoke once it reads InService.
print(sm_endpoint_status(ep))

# 4) Invoke it LIVE on raw rows. Two equivalent ways:
rows = read_athena("SELECT * FROM <your_table> LIMIT 10")

# a) predict() auto-routes a SageMakerEndpoint handle to the remote call — identical
#    code to scoring a local model.
labels = predict(ep, rows)
print("labels:", labels)

# b) sm_predict() is the explicit remote call (handle OR 'microvm-ep-...' name string).
#    proba=True returns class probabilities for ranking by likelihood.
probs = sm_predict(ep, rows, proba=True)
print("probabilities:", probs)

# 5) CLEAN UP — an endpoint is the one standing resource here. Delete it when done;
#    this removes the endpoint, its config, and the model in one call. Serverless is
#    $0 idle, but don't leave resources lying around.
print(sm_delete_endpoint(ep))

### Want always-warm instead? (instance endpoint)

Swap step 2 for `sm_deploy_instance` when you need no cold start or a specific/GPU instance type. It **bills continuously while running**, so it gains a stop/start lifecycle:

```python
ep = sm_deploy_instance(model, instance_type="ml.m5.large")  # dedicated, always-warm
predict(ep, rows)                                            # same invoke contract
sm_stop_endpoint(ep)    # tear down the running endpoint → $0, KEEP config + model
sm_start_endpoint(ep)   # recreate it from the retained config (a few min to InService)
sm_delete_endpoint(ep)  # PERMANENT teardown when you're truly done
```

In the **Data Sources** panel, an instance endpoint shows an **Instance** badge (serverless shows **Serverless**) with **Stop/Start** buttons; a stopped one shows a grey **Stopped** dot until you start it. `sm_stop_endpoint` is a no-op on a serverless endpoint (nothing to stop — it's already $0 idle).
